blocks.text: DEMOLITION FAQ
Demolition Services in Vaughan — What to Know Before You Book

items.q: How much does demolition cost in Vaughan?
a: Price depends on the structure — a fence section or trampoline is a small job; a full above ground pool, garage or concrete pad costs more given the size, material and crew time involved. The exact figure is confirmed free at the walkthrough and covers teardown, haul-away and disposal together, with per-project pricing available for builders.

items.q: Can you coordinate demolition directly with our contractor's schedule?
a: Yes — it’s regular work for us in Vaughan. Removal books against your project’s sequence like any other trade, with a committed date that holds, and per-project pricing for contractors and renovation companies clearing multiple structures.

items.q: Do you handle pool demolition ahead of a bigger backyard project?
a: Regularly. Above ground pool demolition — frame, liner and decking — gets timed to land before your landscaper, patio installer or in-ground pool crew arrives, so the site is ready when they show up.

items.q: Can you demolish a pool house or larger structure in Kleinburg?
a: Yes — larger estate properties are familiar work for us. Pool houses and grounds structures come down with discreet scheduling and the same care given to everything else on the property.

items.q: What's involved in concrete or flooring demolition?
a: The pad, driveway or patio surface gets broken up with equipment matched to its thickness and reinforcement, then hauled off in manageable pieces. The site is left level and cleared, ready for whatever’s next.

items.q: Can demolition happen the same day I call?
a: Often, yes. Trucks run Vaughan daily, 6AM to 11PM, seven days a week, so a morning call frequently means an afternoon demolition — call +1 647 922 5865 for today’s real availability.

items.q: Do builders get standing arrangements for demolition across multiple properties?
a: Readily. A season of projects runs under one quote structure and per-project invoicing, with a crew that already knows your standards and site rules by the second job.

items.q: What happens to the materials after demolition?
a: Metal components go to recyclers, and wood, concrete and other materials are disposed of responsibly. Nothing goes to landfill that has a better destination.

items.q: Why are your demolition rates lower than the bigger companies?
a: No franchise royalty built into the quote — Live Junk Free is local and independent, with our own insured crew and trucks. The identical demolition job, handled just as reliably, simply costs less.
